profiles.meeting_scenario: A coordination meeting between a national greenhouse gas inventory team and a software integration partner preparing this year's inventory submission package based on the 2006 IPCC Guidelines. The immediate context is that the inventory lead needs the energy-sector calculation workbook and the reporting tables to line up before the internal review window opens next week. The agenda is to align on what the '2006 IPCC-aligned package' will include, which workbook version the software team should ingest, how the QA-ready status will be signaled, and who will update the shared emission factor reference sheet used across sectors. The expected outcome is a seemingly clear handoff plan for files, statuses, and ownership so both teams can proceed without further meetings.

members.name: Elena Petrov
members.expertise: Energy-sector greenhouse gas accounting, IPCC category mapping, national inventory compilation
members.background: Elena has led stationary combustion and transport estimates for the country's annual UNFCCC submission for six years and works primarily in the inventory team's spreadsheet-based compilation process.
members.private_state: Elena wants to keep the energy chapter on schedule without reopening category calculations that were already signed off internally, and she is worried that the software integration team may inadvertently pull in draft factors or force formatting changes too late in the cycle.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the '2006 IPCC-aligned package,' they mean category calculations and reporting structure based on the 2006 volumes, while country-specific emission factors and existing notation keys stay as already maintained in the current national workbook.
The 'latest workbook' is the latest reviewed file in the inventory team's shared drive, which is the version with comments resolved up to the internal energy review on Monday morning.
A file marked 'QA-ready' means calculation logic is stable enough for cross-sector consistency checks, even if memo items, notation keys, and cell-level annotations are still being cleaned up.
The shared emission factor reference sheet is owned by the inventory team, and downstream users can mirror it but should not directly edit the master during the submission cycle.

members.name: Marcus Lee
members.expertise: Environmental reporting systems, data pipelines, tabular schema mapping, audit trail configuration
members.background: Marcus manages the contractor team that converts sector workbooks into the reporting database and submission tables used by the ministry's review and archiving workflow.
members.private_state: Marcus wants to minimize manual remapping this week and ensure the import process can run cleanly through the review platform, and he is concerned about last-minute spreadsheet edits that break auditability.
hidden_assumptions: When people say the '2006 IPCC-aligned package,' they mean not only category structure but also the current reporting-table conventions, notation-key placement, and import schema fields expected by the reporting platform.
The 'latest workbook' is whichever file is most recently saved in the Teams project folder, because that is the integration source designated for automated pickup.
A file marked 'QA-ready' means ready for platform ingestion with stable tabs, references, notation keys, and metadata fields, so no structural changes should occur afterward.

The shared emission factor reference sheet is a jointly maintained operational artifact; if his team updates unit labels or factor IDs needed for import, those edits count as routine maintenance rather than ownership changes.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the '2006 IPCC-aligned package'
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to finalize the '2006 IPCC-aligned package' for handoff.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the energy calculations and reporting categories are aligned to the 2006 IPCC Guidelines volumes, with the existing national workbook conventions left intact unless a methodological issue is found.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the handoff bundle also includes all spreadsheet structures and metadata fields needed to conform to the reporting platform's current import schema built around 2006-IPCC category reporting.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both regularly use '2006 IPCC-aligned' as a reassuring shorthand for compliance, and because each sees their own additions as obvious implementation detail rather than an extra scope item, neither hears a mismatch.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Marcus will ingest 'the latest workbook' after the meeting.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena is referring to Energy_v12_reviewed.xlsx on the inventory shared drive, the last internally reviewed workbook with stable formulas.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus is referring to Energy_v13_draft.xlsx in the Teams folder, the most recently modified file that his automation monitors.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In both teams, 'latest' is routinely used without file names because there is usually a single active artifact; here there are parallel repositories, but that detail feels too mundane to restate.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree Elena will mark the workbook 'QA-ready' before the handoff window.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena means the emissions values and formula logic are ready for substantive QA, even if tabs for notation keys and explanatory comments are still being tidied.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus means the file is fully ingestion-ready, with frozen tab names, complete notation keys, locked references, and no expected structural edits after upload.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: QA status sounds like a standard maturity marker, and both assume the other uses the same internal gate definition because each organization has long-established review workflows.

misalignment_points.topic: Ownership of the shared emission factor reference sheet
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that Marcus's team can 'update the factor reference sheet' so the package stays synchronized.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Elena assumes Marcus's team will copy values or propose edits while the inventory team remains the only group directly modifying the master factor sheet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Marcus assumes his team can directly edit the shared master sheet to normalize IDs, units, and labels required by the import process.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both see the update as minor maintenance work rather than a decision about control of a shared artifact, so the phrase 'update the sheet' passes as operationally obvious.

From my side, the 2006 IPCC-aligned package just means the energy categories and calculation set are aligned to the 2006 Guidelines structure we've already been compiling against, with our existing workbook conventions left alone. If we can hand that off cleanly, we stay on track for the internal review next week.
